# Third-party, real-world fixtures

**These five documents are not ours and were not generated by this repository.** Every
other fixture under `tests/fixtures/` outside `samplelib/` and this directory is written
by a committed `tools/make_*.py` script; these were supplied by the user as a wider
real-world test of the cascade and the vertical model, and are kept apart so that the
distinction stays visible.

| --- | --- |

- **Source:** <https://word.to/samples/docx/>
- **Downloaded:** 2026-09-24
- **Terms** (the same page, checked on 2026-09-24, verbatim): *"every sample file is
  generated programmatically and is free to download and use for any purpose —
  personal, commercial, or educational"* and *"The samples are generated
  programmatically. Nothing in them is copyrighted, so no attribution is needed."* No
  attribution is required; this note is kept anyway.
- **Contents checked before committing:** no embedded fonts (no `word/fonts/` part), no
  font data of any kind; one PNG figure (`sample-with-images`) and a JPEG thumbnail each.

What they are, as far as the files say: `docProps/app.xml` names Microsoft Macintosh
Word 14, and the styles, theme and `settings.xml` (`compatibilityMode` 14,
`w:useFELayout`, `overrideTableStyleFontSizeAndJustification`) are the same Word for Mac
2011 template as `../samplelib/` (theme major Calibri, minor Cambria; Courier named
twice). The bodies were written programmatically on that template. The names are the
generator's, not Word's: Word lays `sample-5pages` out on **one** page and
`sample-10pages` on **three**. Neither has a single explicit page break -- the two page
breaks of `sample-10pages` are Word's own, the first natural breaks in any fixture here.

Word's exports of them are not committed (a PDF carries font subsets). Their measured
baselines are, in `../baseline-observations.json`.
